claims.head: Quality over quantity for the Canadiens
claims.call: The Canadiens’ average shot has at least their usual 6.9% chance of going in.
claims.body: The Capitals have struggled to prevent dangerous shots, and the Canadiens don’t waste many.
claims.nums: Montréal 2nd for shot quality (a 6.9% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Washington 28th for preventing dangerous shots
claims.gist: The Canadiens make their shots count, and the Capitals allow dangerous ones.

check.measure: the average shot’s chance of going in, by expected goals
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Forecheck against patience
claims.body: The Canadiens are around the middle of the league for forecheck pressure, at the hounding end; the Capitals are near the bottom of the league, at the passive end. Expect that gap to show.
claims.gist: The Canadiens and the Capitals sit at opposite ends for forecheck pressure.
claims.call: The Canadiens put more forecheck pressure on than the Capitals.

notes.text: O. Kapanen is day to day (lower body injury) and has not played this season. J. Slafkovský has taken his spot beside A. Newhook and I. Demidov.
K. Guhle is expected back after missing 4 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
A. Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 27% of the team’s shorthanded time in 4 games, up from 6% last season.
M. Roy is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-four defenseman. T. Liljegren has taken his spot beside J. Chychrun.

WSH.head: A genuine toss-up
WSH.body: Montréal has had more of the chances over recent games and Washington has home ice. Washington can tip it if they get good looks.

MTL.head: Nothing to separate these two
MTL.body: Montréal has had more of the chances over recent games and Washington has home ice. Montréal can tip it if they get good looks.
